- If sentiment shows negative spikes (e.g., -0.50, -0.20) followed by a rebound, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope after such events.
- When true outcome shows sharp upward moves (e.g., >90) followed by steep declines, model often fails to anticipate the reversal — cap forecast peak at 10% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive (0.00) and model shows steady upward trend, true outcome often diverges downward — introduce early mean reversion bias (e.g., reduce forecast by 1–2% per 3-day horizon).
- Model consistently overestimates short-term spikes (e.g., 89.76 → 90.79) and underestimates long-term decline (e.g., 96.93 → 68.49) — apply horizon-dependent decay: 30d forecasts should be capped at 10% below 30d high if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment history includes a recent positive value (e.g., 0.33), model often overreacts — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 5 days if sentiment is positive.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in early days — if sentiment changes from 0.00 to -0.20 or 0.20 within 3 days, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift (e.g., reduce slope if sentiment turns negative).
